summary: Code review completed across all 10 migrated test classes (tests/DOM/, tests/Selectors/, tests/Parsing/). 209 tests / 1014 assertions confirmed passing at exit 0.
No blocking issues found. The migration is architecturally sound, well-isolated, and follows PHPUnit best practices throughout.

Maintainability: All classes use declare(strict_types=1), consistent PSR-4 namespacing (Tests\DOM, Tests\Selectors, Tests\Parsing), section comments for scanability, and descriptive test method names — all strong.

Test isolation: setUp()/tearDown() correctly calls ->clear() then unset() for shared fixtures. Classes using locally-scoped $dom (ReaderElementTest, ReaderSelectorTest) call ->clear() at the end of each test. Pattern is consistent.
Best practices: DataProvider used in StandardTest for monkey tests — significantly better than the original mt_rand() loop. Each data point is now individually identified on failure.
Security: No security concerns applicable to a test-only migration. Library src/ untouched (confirmed via QA git diff).
Non-blocking observations documented in comments.

metrics.test_coverage: 10 PHPUnit test classes covering all 10 legacy testcase files

comments.note: MiscTest::testErrorTagHandling creates a local $dom via str_get_html() and calls $dom->clear() at method end. If any assertion before the final line fails, $dom->clear() is never called and circular references are left for PHP GC. Pattern is inconsistent with the setUp/tearDown fixture used by the rest of the class. Consider wrapping in try/finally or moving to a separate test class that uses setUp/tearDown exclusively.

SelectorTest and ReaderSelectorTest share near-identical test scenarios (testTabNewlineInTag, testClassSelector, testIdSelector, testAttrSelector, testTextSelector, testXmlNamespaceSelector). Duplication is justified given the two separate legacy origins, but a future refactor could extract common assertions into a shared abstract base class or trait to reduce maintenance surface.

phpunit.xml has no <source> element pointing to src/. Running --coverage-html or --coverage-text will produce incomplete or empty reports. For CI integration, add <source><include><directory>src/</directory></include></source> to phpunit.xml.

CallbackTest::testCallbackAddAttribute uses a discarded (string) $this->dom; expression to trigger the first callback's side-effects before setting the second callback. This relies on the library's __toString() triggering the callback pass. The comment explains the reasoning clearly, but the technique is fragile: any change to the library's lazy-evaluation strategy would silently break this test without a PHP error. Consider using an explicit ->save() call (which is semantically clearer) or a dedicated trigger method if one exists.

Gold Nugget — StandardTest::testChemistryFormula documents a genuine silent-loss bug in the library: '<1 mol%...' content after the broken tag opener is silently discarded. The original legacy assert() was passing silently because PHP assert() was not configured to throw. This is now correctly documented as a known non-round-trip edge case with assertIsString. This finding is valuable and should be tracked as a follow-up WP to either fix the library or add this to a documented known-limitations list.

Gold Nugget — The DataProvider pattern in StandardTest::monkeyStringProvider is architecturally excellent. Named data sets make each edge-case individually identifiable in PHPUnit output, replacing the original opaque mt_rand() loop. This pattern should be applied to any future parametrised tests added to this suite.
